title: T3c: Correct IAM grant, resource-policy, and endpoint-import review findings
description:
Purpose: correct the confirmed findings of the independent T1–T3b implementation review before T4 builds on them. Design: docs/designs/lambda-web-functions-integration.md REVISION 4. Authoritative sections: §8 (namespace note), §8.3 (reserved child IDs, read-only Endpoints, execution-role ordering), §8.4 (AddToResourcePolicy restrictions, imported-endpoint validation and account rule), §10.2 (updated table + "Revision 4 corrections" items 1–6), §10.3 (statement integrity), §12.1, §14 (revision-4 rows), §15 (revision-4 additions), §21 revision 4.

Implement revision 4 exactly. If any rule cannot be implemented as written (for example a CDK public API behaves differently from what the design states), STOP and record a blocker with bd update <id> --append-notes. Do not change the design yourself.

Deliverables (files: WebFunctionGrants.cs, WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.cs, WebFunctionImportedEndpoint.cs, WebFunctionConstruct.cs, Models/WebFunctionEndpoint.cs → move, tests):

1. F1 Service principals (§10.2 rev-4 item 1). GrantInvoke throws InvalidOperationException for any principal whose PolicyFragment.PrincipalJson is a "Service" principal (bare ServicePrincipal or PrincipalWithConditions wrapping one), under BOTH CallerPolicy values. The service name is a token in CDK 2.274, so resolve it (Stack.Of(endpoint).Resolve) to detect cloudfront.amazonaws.com. Remedy text: CloudFront → "use GrantCloudFrontInvoke(distributionArn)"; other services → "add an explicit, condition-scoped statement with endpoint.AddToResourcePolicy(...)". Do NOT add aws:SourceAccount automatically. Do NOT add a new public API for scoped service grants (deferred).
2. Wildcards (§10.2 rev-4 item 2; §8.4).
   - GrantInvoke throws InvalidOperationException for EVERY wildcard principal (PrincipalJson AWS="*" or LiteralString="*"; AnyPrincipal, StarPrincipal, OrganizationPrincipal, conditioned or not) under both CallerPolicy values. Remedy text: use an explicit, conditioned AddToResourcePolicy statement.
   - AddToResourcePolicy rejects (ArgumentException) Allow statements that have no conditions and name a wildcard or service principal, and Allow statements using NotPrincipal.
   - Deny statements are unrestricted.
   - An explicit Allow with a wildcard AND conditions is accepted. Check only that conditions are present; do NOT build any IAM-condition analyzer. XML docs state the consumer is responsible for the conditions meaningfully restricting access.
   - GrantCloudFrontInvoke (conditioned) keeps working.
3. F3 Account principals (§10.2 rev-4 item 3). AccountPrincipal and AccountRootPrincipal (by .NET type), and any principal whose LITERAL AWS principal is an account root ARN, are never established. Automatic throws, even for the same account. ExternallyManaged behavior unchanged.
4. P1 Verified identity writes (§10.2 rev-4 item 4) for owned AND imported principals. The identity side counts as written only when (a) the grant principal is a concrete owned mutable CDK identity (.NET Amazon.CDK.AWS.IAM.Role, User, Group, or LazyRole with Resource.IsOwnedResource == true), or (b) AddToPrincipalPolicy returned StatementAdded == true with PolicyDependable is Amazon.CDK.AWS.IAM.Policy (replacing the current "is IConstruct" check). Everything else is not written: fallback to the resource statement on an owned endpoint, throw on an imported endpoint. Never infer a write from Grant.PrincipalStatements. Verified facts on 2.274.0: an owned Role returns an EMPTY DependencyGroup (so signal (b) alone would break owned roles); ImmutableRole returns an empty DependencyGroup; imported mutable role/user/group return Policy; a classic Function's role, LazyRole, and User surface as concrete .NET types; owned.WithoutPolicyUpdates() surfaces as an IPrincipal proxy (not Role).
5. F2 Role dependency (§8.3 notes, §12.1). Replace _revision.Node.AddDependency(Role) with a dependency on the role's CfnRole only (Role.Node.DefaultChild when it is a CfnResource; nothing extra for imported roles; ExecutionRoleArn already references the role). Never depend on the DefaultPolicy subtree. Keep every other DependsOn edge (Function, created LogGroup, bucket PolicyDependable).
6. F5 Imported endpoints (§8.4; public API addition approved by the maintainer).
   - Add `public string? Account { get; init; }` to WebFunctionEndpointAttributes, with XML docs.
   - Validation:
     - a literal EndpointArn must match arn:{p}:lambda:{r}:{12 digits}:web-function/{fn}/endpoint/{ep} (ArgumentException);
     - a literal DomainName must be non-empty (null → ArgumentNullException, empty → ArgumentException);
     - a literal Account must be 12 digits;
     - when Account and the ARN are both literal, they must be equal (ArgumentException);
     - tokens are not validated.
   - Environment: Env.Account = the literal ARN account, else Account; Env.Region from the ARN. Use ResourceProps.EnvironmentFromArn, or explicit Account/Region if CDK does not allow combining them. Assert the result in tests either way.
   - Endpoint account = the literal ARN account, else a literal Account; anything else is NOT established.
   - If the endpoint account is not established, GrantInvoke throws for EVERY grantee, owned included (this replaces the revision-3 owned-only rule and its annotation). The message names both remedies (supply a literal Account; configure caller access outside this app) and notes that the endpoint remains usable as a CloudFront origin with ExternallyManaged origin permissions.
   - If the endpoint account is established, a grantee is established only when its account is literally SAME (owned → its stack account; imported → PrincipalAccount). ONE_UNRESOLVED and BOTH_UNRESOLVED are not established.
   - Constructing an imported endpoint with a token ARN and no Account must succeed; it must not throw at FromEndpointAttributes.
7. P6 Statement integrity (§10.3). AddToResourcePolicy validates, then stores statement.Copy() with Freeze() applied. WebFunctionConstruct registers a node validation that returns PolicyDocument.ValidateForResourcePolicy() errors for the resource policy (when one exists). Keep StatementAdded/PolicyDependable return semantics.
8. P3 Reserved ids (§8.3). AddEndpoint throws ArgumentException for the ids Function, Revision, DefaultEndpoint, ExecutionRole, LogGroup, ResourcePolicy (ordinal).
9. Endpoints read-only. Return a cached ReadOnlyCollection (or equivalent) that cannot be cast back to a mutable List; the public type stays IReadOnlyList<WebFunctionEndpointConstruct>.
10. F4 Diagnostics (§10.2 rev-4 item 6). Errors and annotations identify the grantee by the IGrantable's construct path when it is an IConstruct (jsii IRole proxies are), else the principal's resolved policy-fragment JSON, else the type name. Identify the endpoint by construct path + EndpointName, never by an ARN token. No human-facing text contains "${Token[". The ExternallyManaged annotation describes caller-side identity policies only for IAM identities.
11. Namespace (§8 rev-4 note). Move IWebFunctionEndpoint to namespace LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs, in file IWebFunctionEndpoint.cs at the project root. XML docs state it is not intended for consumer implementation. Also correct the stale WebFunctionConstruct XML summary ("added by later releases").

Regression tests (WebFunctionInvokeGrantTests / WebFunctionResourcePolicyTests / WebFunctionConstructTests; [Collection("CDK Tests")]; assert on templates and messages, not on internals):
- Service principals: cloudfront (message names GrantCloudFrontInvoke), another service, and a conditioned one each throw under Automatic AND ExternallyManaged; no ResourcePolicy synthesized.
- Wildcards:
  - GrantInvoke with AnyPrincipal, StarPrincipal, and a conditioned OrganizationPrincipal throws under BOTH policies; no ResourcePolicy is created.
  - AddToResourcePolicy: an unconditioned "*" Allow throws; Allow+NotPrincipal throws; a Deny with "*" is accepted; an explicit Allow with "*" plus an aws:PrincipalOrgID StringEquals condition writes exactly that statement (condition preserved).
- Same-account AccountPrincipal and AccountRootPrincipal under Automatic throw.
- No-op identity writes (real CDK types, no fakes): Role.FromRoleArn(Mutable=false); Mutable=false + AddGrantsToResources=true; owned.WithoutPolicyUpdates(). Each → resource statement with the role ARN principal, ZERO AWS::IAM::Policy, and returned Grant.PrincipalStatements empty; the same grantees on an imported endpoint throw.
- Real identity policies: owned Role, classic Lambda Function, WebFunctionConstruct, mutable imported role, imported User, imported Group → exactly one AWS::IAM::Policy statement with Action lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint and Resource = that endpoint's ARN, attached to the right role/user/group; no ResourcePolicy.
- Unresolved imported ARNs: token role ARN (Fn.ImportValue) and a literal role ARN in an env-agnostic stack under Automatic → throw, zero AWS::IAM::Policy.
- Imported endpoints:
  - Throw at FromEndpointAttributes: an invalid literal ARN (a function ARN, a missing endpoint segment); null and empty DomainName; a non-12-digit Account; an Account that differs from a literal ARN's account.
  - A literal ARN with an equal Account is accepted.
  - Env.Account/Env.Region equal the endpoint's (literal ARN; token ARN + literal Account).
  - A literal foreign ARN with an owned caller in an env-agnostic stack throws.
  - A token ARN with no Account: construction succeeds, and GrantInvoke throws for an owned Role AND for an imported mutable role, with ZERO AWS::IAM::Policy.
  - A token ARN with a literal Account equal to the caller stack's account and an owned caller writes the identity policy.
  - A token ARN with a literal Account different from the caller's account throws.
  - An immutable same-account role on an imported endpoint throws.
- CDK upgrade guard: group the real-CDK principal-behavior tests (no-op writes, real identity policies, service/wildcard/account classification) in a clearly named class or trait (e.g. CdkPrincipalBehaviorRegressionTests). Its class doc comment states that these pin CDK/jsii behavior observed in 2.274.0 and that a failure on an Amazon.CDK.Lib upgrade blocks the upgrade until the signals are re-verified (design §10.2 rev-4 item 4).
- Diagnostics: error messages contain the grantee construct path (imported role id), EndpointName, and both remedies; annotations asserted via Annotations.FromStack (info level, expected text); no message or annotation contains "${Token[".
- Cycles: mutual invocation (A↔B), self-invocation, and BFF/API (API env var = web.DefaultEndpoint.Url, api.DefaultEndpoint.GrantInvoke(web)) → Template.FromStack succeeds. Assert that the revision DependsOn contains the CfnRole logical id and does NOT contain any DefaultPolicy id.
- Statement integrity: mutating the caller's statement after AddToResourcePolicy (AddResources("*")) leaves the template unchanged; a principal-less statement fails synthesis validation; the GrantInvoke resource path renders exactly one statement (dedupe of the double add).
- Reserved ids: each reserved id passed to AddEndpoint throws ArgumentException. Endpoints: casting to List<T>/ICollection<T> mutation fails.
- Replace the existing StatementAdded=false regression so it exercises a GrantInvoke-level path where feasible; keep a direct test of the internal helper only as a supplement.

Golden templates (§12.4): the revision-dependency change intentionally alters web-function-use-log-group.json (SuppliedRoleDefaultPolicy… drops from the Revision DependsOn) and possibly other goldens whose role has a DefaultPolicy. Regenerate ONLY affected files with UPDATE_GOLDEN_TEMPLATES=1, then review every diff line. Record in the bead notes each changed golden, the exact changed lines, and why. Any diff beyond DependsOn removal of DefaultPolicy ids is a defect. The 17 existing-construct goldens must remain byte-identical. Add one new golden: a mutual-invocation pair + an explicit conditioned-wildcard AddToResourcePolicy statement (aws:PrincipalOrgID).

Required synthesis validation (record commands and results in notes): from the repo root, run dotnet restore LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx; dotnet build LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx -c Release (0 warnings); and dotnet test --solution LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx -c Release across net8.0–net11.0 (JSII_SILENCE_WARNING_UNTESTED_NODE_VERSION=1). Then grep src/ for AddToPrincipalOrResource|\.Success\b|AssertSuccess (must be empty) and for PrincipalStatements.Length used as write evidence (must be absent).

Exclusions: WebFunctionOrigin/T4; Testing-namespace helpers; user docs (T6a/T6b); owned-bucket inspection and DSSE (separate follow-up bead); existing constructs; any AWS deployment. No commits or pushes unless separately authorized.

Security: never synthesize an unconditioned service-principal or wildcard Allow statement; never report a grant as complete when no policy was verifiably written; never write an identity policy for a principal whose account is not literally established for an imported endpoint.
acceptance_criteria:

• GrantInvoke rejects all service principals (CloudFront remedy → GrantCloudFrontInvoke) and ALL wildcard principals, conditioned or not, under both CallerPolicy values.

• Identity writes are counted only by the two revision-4 signals, for owned and imported principals. ImmutableRole, AddGrantsToResources=true, and WithoutPolicyUpdates() never produce a silent no-op (real-CDK tests, zero AWS::IAM::Policy). Unestablished authorization fails closed.
• The real-CDK principal-behavior regression tests are grouped as a named CDK-upgrade guard whose doc comment cites the 2.274.0 observations and the upgrade-blocking rule.
• Mutual, self, and BFF/API invocation patterns synthesize; the revision depends on the CfnRole and never on a DefaultPolicy.
• WebFunctionEndpointAttributes.Account (string?) exists.
• Literal ARN, domain, and Account are validated, and Account must match a literal ARN.
• Env is the endpoint's.
• GrantInvoke throws for every grantee when the endpoint account is not established (token ARN without a literal Account), and constructing such an endpoint still succeeds.
• For an established endpoint account, only literal SAME grantee accounts are established.
• Stored resource-policy statements are frozen copies; ValidateForResourcePolicy runs at synthesis; reserved AddEndpoint ids are rejected; Endpoints is genuinely read-only; IWebFunctionEndpoint lives in LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.
• Errors and annotations name the grantee and endpoint meaningfully and never contain ${Token[; annotations are asserted in tests.
• Golden changes are limited to the intentional DependsOn removals (each diff recorded and explained in notes) plus the one new golden; the 17 existing-construct goldens are unchanged.
• Release build has 0 warnings; the full suite passes on net8.0–net11.0; grep checks are clean; evidence is recorded in notes.

HOW DOCUMENT VALIDATION WAS IMPLEMENTED (Option B, transactional): WebFunctionConstruct.AddResourcePolicyStatement(statement):
1. WebFunctionValidation.ValidateResourcePolicyStatement(statement) (revision-4 security checks: Deny allowed; Allow+NotPrincipal rejected; Allow with conditions accepted; otherwise Allow naming a service or wildcard principal rejected).
2. var stored = statement.Copy(null); stored.Freeze();
3. Build a candidate: new PolicyDocument(new PolicyDocumentProps { Statements = [.. _resourcePolicyStatements, stored] }).
4. var errors = candidate.ValidateForResourcePolicy(null); if errors.Length > 0 throw InvalidOperationException($"The resource policy for Web Function '{Node.Path}' is invalid: {string.Join("; ", errors)}").
5. Only after validation: append to a private List<PolicyStatement> _resourcePolicyStatements, lazily create the single real _resourcePolicy PolicyDocument + single AWS::Lambda::CfnResourcePolicy child id "ResourcePolicy" (ResourceArn = _function.AttrFunctionArn).
Every subsequent addition revalidates the COMPLETE candidate document (no invalid partial state is applied). Single-policy ownership, endpoint-scoped resources, wildcard/service checks, and Deny behavior are preserved.

R1 - ELIMINATED MUTATION-BASED IDENTITY PROBING. WebFunctionGrants no longer calls AddToPrincipalPolicy as a capability probe. Deleted IdentityPolicyCanBeWritten (it wrote an unconditional identity Allow via PrincipalWithConditions and then fell back, bypassing conditions). Identity writes are now decided by pure type classification: IsOwnedMutableIdentity(principal) = principal is Amazon.CDK.AWS.IAM.Role/User/Group/LazyRole AND Resource.IsOwnedResource == true. Added RejectUnsupportedPrincipalWrapper(principal, endpointName): any PrincipalWithConditions is rejected with InvalidOperationException BEFORE any policy mutation. Grant.PrincipalStatements / Grant.Success / AssertSuccess / AddToPrincipalOrResource are not used anywhere.

R2 - CONDITIONED AccountPrincipal BYPASS CLOSED. Replaced IsAccountRootArn with IsAccountRootOrId (recurse IEnumerable (PrincipalJson values are arrays); string: fail-literal when it is an account-root ARN (arn:...:root) OR a 12-digit account id; unresolved tokens not matched). IsAccountPrincipal still keys off the concrete .NET types AccountPrincipal/AccountRootPrincipal first. Account/account-root principals are never established: Automatic throws even same-account, ExternallyManaged writes only a resource statement.

CONSEQUENCE / REQUIRED DESIGN CLARIFICATION (report; do NOT edit design): a mutable imported role and an immutable imported role are indistinguishable via jsii (both IRole._Proxy/IPrincipal._Proxy, is Role false, IsOwnedResource false). KEY CORRECTNESS FINDING (fixed): Role.FromRoleArn(..., Mutable=false) returns an ImmutableRole whose AddToPrincipalPolicy returns StatementAdded=true while writing NOTHING (CDK pretendSuccess = !addGrantsToResources). Grant.AddToPrincipal therefore reports a non-empty PrincipalStatements for an immutable imported role, so trusting PrincipalStatements.Length caused a SILENT NO-OP (no identity, no resource statement). Detection now probes grantee.GrantPrincipal.AddToPrincipalPolicy(principal-less statement) and treats the identity as written only when result.StatementAdded && result.PolicyDependable is IConstruct (a real Policy for a mutable imported role; a bare DependencyGroup for an immutable one). title: T2 follow-up: Harden owned code-bucket inspection (tokens, unrecognized values, DSSE classification)
description:
Purpose: align WebFunctionCodeFromBucket.ValidateOwnedBucketConfiguration (src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Models/WebFunctionCode.cs) with design §14 and the revision-4 clarification under the §14 table. Source: independent review findings P4 and DSSE.

Defects:
(1) Tokens are rejected instead of skipped: a VersioningConfiguration.Status token resolves to {Ref:...}, its ToString() is compared to 'Enabled', and the bucket is rejected.
(2) A Stack.Resolve result whose structure is not recognized should be treated as unknown and skipped, not rejected.
(3) UsesAwsManagedKey rejects every aws:kms:dsse bucket, including DSSE with a customer-managed key. Per §8.7/§14, reject only DSSE_MANAGED (no key) and KMS_MANAGED/aws/s3, and make each message name the actual problem.
(4) Versioning enabled only through an escape-hatch property override is a documented limitation, not a fix target. T6a documents the workaround (Bucket.FromBucketName + ExternallyManaged).

Keep the current rule that owned buckets are inspected even under ExternallyManaged; the design does not change that.

Tests: token Status skipped; DSSE with a customer key accepted; DSSE_MANAGED rejected with an accurate message; KMS_MANAGED still rejected; customer-key SSE-KMS accepted; unversioned still rejected.

Exclusions: IAM/grant code (T3c), docs (T6a). No golden changes expected; verify. No commits or pushes unless authorized.
acceptance_criteria:
• Unresolved bucket configuration values are handled conservatively: a token or unrecognized versioning Status, encryption algorithm, encryption structure, or KMS key id is SKIPPED and never rejected (each case has a test). Unresolved values are never treated as proof of a violation.
• Literal violations are still rejected: unversioned, KMS_MANAGED/aws/s3, DSSE_MANAGED (no key).
• DSSE with a customer-managed key is accepted. Messages name the actual problem.
• Escape-hatch-only versioning remains a documented limitation (T6a); it is not handled in code.
• New tests pass; all goldens unchanged.
• Release build has 0 warnings and the full suite passes on net8.0–net11.0; evidence is recorded in notes.
notes:
Maintainer decision (2026-10-23): keep escape-hatch S3 versioning as a documented limitation. Handle unresolved values conservatively: never reject tokenized values.
IMPLEMENTATION (2026-10-23): Rewrote WebFunctionCodeFromBucket.ValidateOwnedBucketConfiguration in src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Models/WebFunctionCode.cs into ValidateVersioning + ValidateEncryption + ValidateKmsKey, classifying every value as literal-valid, literal-invalid, or unresolved/unrecognized.

Storage/versioning/encryption handling:
- Versioning: missing VersioningConfiguration or literal Status "Suspended" -> reject (VersioningMessage). Literal Status "Enabled" -> accept. A token Status, a missing status key, a non-dictionary resolved structure, or any other literal status -> skipped (never rejected).
- Encryption: missing BucketEncryption -> no violation. Unrecognized structure (not a map, no rules, no ServerSideEncryptionByDefault) -> skipped. Algorithm literal "aws:kms": key literal aws/s3 or empty/absent -> reject (KmsManagedMessage names aws/s3); literal customer key -> accept; token/absent-as-token key -> skipped (never treated as AWS-managed). Algorithm literal "aws:kms:dsse": no key / aws/s3 -> reject (DsseManagedMessage names customer-managed key); literal customer key -> accept; token key -> skipped. AES256 and any other literal algorithm -> accepted.
- LiteralString helper returns null for a non-string value or a string containing `${Token[`, so resolved tokens are never misread as literals.

Security-policy behavior: ExternallyManaged still inspects owned buckets (versioning/encryption) exactly as before - design §14 row unchanged. The Automatic-only cross-stack account/Region guard and AddToResourcePolicy remain bypassed under ExternallyManaged (no bucket-policy statement is generated). No other semantics changed.

Regression tests added to test/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.Tests/WebFunctionConstructTests.cs (13 new): enabled+S3-managed accepted (asserts synthesized S3::BucketPolicy); disabled (Versioned=false) rejected with versioning message; suspended rejected; tokenized versioning Status skipped (asserts synthesized policy); unrecognized literal versioning Status skipped; AWS-managed KMS (aws/s3) rejected naming aws/s3; customer-managed KMS accepted; tokenized KMS key skipped; DSSE with customer-managed key accepted; DSSE_MANAGED rejected naming customer-managed; DSSE + aws/s3 rejected; unrecognized encryption structure skipped; ExternallyManaged cross-stack owned bucket with unresolved function env does not throw (Automatic-only guard not applied). Existing fixtures retained (owned-bucket policy statements + revision DependsOn on bucket policy, imported-bucket Automatic error, ExternallyManaged no-policy, unversioned, KMS_MANAGED, cross-stack Automatic error). These exercise the real L1 property structs (CfnBucket.VersioningConfigurationProperty / BucketEncryptionProperty) so validation runs against synthesized configuration.

Evidence: dotnet build -c Release -> Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Full suite per TFM (dotnet run --project test/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.Tests/ -c Release --no-build): net8.0/net9.0/net10.0/net11.0 each Total 450, Errors 0, Failed 0, Skipped 0 (was 437 before; +13). All 24 golden templates byte-identical (git reports no GoldenTemplates changes); no golden updates required. dotnet format --verify-no-changes reports no issues in the two changed files. Only two files modified. No commit or push performed (per task restrictions).

Unresolved behavior (documented, not code): versioning enabled solely via an escape-hatch property override is not detected (limitation, T6a workaround); imported buckets remain uninspected.

Unresolved values (token/unrecognized versioning Status, encryption algorithm, KMS key id, encryption structure) are skipped and never rejected; literal violations still rejected (unversioned/Suspended, KMS_MANAGED aws/s3, DSSE_MANAGED); DSSE with a customer-managed key accepted; messages name the actual problem. title: T6a: Write Web Function construct docs, security guidance, and workload recipes
description:
Purpose: user documentation for the constructs and the three workload recipes. Design §16 (AUTHORITATIVE content list), §5 (facts), §10–§12 (security/deployment), §14 (documented-not-validated list), §8.7.

Deliverables:
- docs/constructs/web-function.md: overview; auth modes and who can reach an endpoint (ApplicationManaged is public even behind CloudFront; IamAuth ≠ user auth);
  WebFunctionCode.FromBucket requirements (versioning, s3:GetObject/GetObjectVersion, /revision/* SourceArn statement, optional VersionId semantics, cross-account buckets,
  SSE-KMS key policy, CDK bootstrap bucket incompatibility, object must exist before deploy); WebFunctionLogs (TWO_WEEKS default, ONE_MONTH example, ServiceDefault no expiry);
  endpoints/AddEndpoint and revision-change behavior; GrantInvoke table from §10.2 incl. ExternallyManaged contract and caller-side SigV4 (service lambda, UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD,
  Authorization stripping); single-owner resource-policy contract; WebFunctionOrigin (OAC, same-stack rule, ExternallyManaged, imported endpoints);
  cache/header guidance (§11.3: never forward Host / use ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER, Authorization in cache policy, Lambda@Edge origin triggers rejected, opt-in Regions 403);
  replacement table (§12.2); validation errors (§14); KMS deferral + unsupported escape hatch (§8.7); limitations.
- Workload recipes (same page or docs/examples/web-functions.md): Next.js standalone; ASP.NET Core via Node.js execve shim (self-contained linux-arm64 apphost "server", index.js
  `process.execve("/var/task/server", ["/var/task/server"], process.env);`, Kestrel on http://$AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT, readiness POST to
  http://$AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API/2025-09-01/ready after start, app-local ICU or invariant globalization, no HTTPS redirection/HSTS); Blazor Static SSR (same shim; untrimmed server;
  ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory when AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT is set; wwwroot/_framework shipped; cache fingerprinted assets; Interactive Server/Auto/legacy Blazor Server
  UNSUPPORTED — WebSockets rejected). Mark execve/readiness as not documented by AWS. Reference https://github.com/j-d-ha/lambda-web-function-not-node.
- mkdocs.yml nav entry under Constructs (and examples page if created). Do NOT add the design doc to nav.
- docs/examples/index.md: §9 examples.

Exclusions: README/CHANGELOG/testing docs (separate bead); no code changes.
Validation: `uv run mkdocs build --clean` succeeds; every code sample matches the implemented public API (cross-check against src/).
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/constructs/web-function.md and recipes cover every §16 item, including security callouts and the §10.2 grant table.
- Three workload recipes are complete and explicitly distinguish Blazor Static SSR from Interactive Server.
- mkdocs nav updated; mkdocs build succeeds; samples match the real API.
notes:
Also document (derived from design §8.2 + §12.1, found during planning): with WebFunctionCodeBucketPolicy.Automatic the code object must exist before the revision is created, so in practice the owned bucket must live in a separately deployed stack (deploy bucket stack -> upload artifact -> deploy function stack). A bucket created in the same stack as the function cannot be pre-populated.
REVIEW ROUTING (2026-10-23, design revision 4). Add to docs/constructs/web-function.md:
(1) Log-group switching: moving an EXISTING function from WebFunctionLogs.ServiceDefault() to Create(), or redeploying after stack deletion while /aws/lambda/web/{name} still exists, fails with AlreadyExists because Lambda auto-creates the group. Document the remedies: Use(LogGroup.FromLogGroupName(...)), or delete/import the group.
(2) CDK 2.274 emits F3006 'Unknown resource type AWS::Lambda::WebFunction*' validation warnings, which become synthesis ERRORS when @aws-cdk/core:validateAgainstDefaultRules is enabled. Document the acknowledgement IDs (CloudFormation-Validate::F3006) and the consequence.
(3) GrantInvoke rejects service principals (CloudFront → GrantCloudFrontInvoke; other services → explicit condition-scoped AddToResourcePolicy) and unconditioned wildcards; same-account AccountPrincipal is not 'complete'.
(4) The revision no longer waits for execution-role DefaultPolicy statements; a brief IAM-propagation window can occur on first deploy.
(5) Owned-bucket limitation: versioning enabled only by an escape-hatch override is not detected; workaround Bucket.FromBucketName + ExternallyManaged.
(6) IWebFunctionEndpoint is not intended for consumer implementation.
Maintainer clarification (2026-10-23):
(7) Conditioned wildcard resource-policy statements are supported only through explicit AddToResourcePolicy. The consumer is responsible for ensuring the conditions meaningfully restrict access; the library checks only that conditions are present.
(8) Imported endpoints: document the optional Account attribute. GrantInvoke needs an established endpoint account (literal ARN or literal Account); a token-ARN endpoint is still usable as an ExternallyManaged OAC origin.

title: T4a (optional): Spike narrow warning for managed AllViewer policy on Web Function origins
description:

(id 216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eafa07d3) using only public CDK APIs on objects the library already holds (e.g. the BehaviorOptions/Origin object identity), WITHOUT resolving
CloudFormation templates, tokens, or CfnDistribution.DistributionConfig?

Rules: disposable spike code first (scratch or a throwaway test); no template-resolution machinery; zero false positives; emits Annotations warning only (never an error).
Outcome A (feasible and simple): implement it within WebFunctionOrigin with tests (warning present for AllViewer; absent for ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER and custom policies).
Outcome B (not feasible): record findings in notes and close as "won't implement"; documentation (cdkc docs bead) already covers the Host-header rule.
Exclusions: Lambda@Edge detection, opt-in Region detection, any IValidation that resolves templates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Findings recorded in notes with the exact approach tried and the decision (A or B).
- If A: warning-only check, tests prove no false positives, golden templates unchanged, validation gates pass.
